title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps

epigraph.quote: Price is what you pay; value is what you get. When a market marks down an accelerating business by more than half, we test whether the multiple was too rich or the cash engine is breaking.
epigraph.author: Institutional Equity Desk Maxim

web_blocks.html: Vertiv Holdings Co. (NYSE: VRT) closed on Friday, November 20, 2026 at $166.24, down 10.14% on the day [47, 48]. The stock sits 56.25% below its $379.94 52-week high and 12.46% above its $147.82 52-week low [47, 48]. At $166.24, basic equity market cap across 385.03 million shares equals $64.01 billion, while Q3 diluted equity value across 392.7 million shares equals $65.28 billion (+$1.27B dilution) [41, 48]. Finviz lists enterprise value at $63.59 billion before October's M&A cash outlay [48]. Adding $1.45 billion of UIG cash shifts net cash ($783.2M at Q3) to $666.8M (~$0.67B) net debt, lifting EV to ~$64.68B basic ($65.95B diluted) [41, 43]. Including $428.4 million in operating leases and $1.42 billion in max contingent earnouts ($239.6M PurgeRite + $29.1M 9M deals + $1,150M UIG; KES undisclosed) lifts full pro-forma EV to $66.52 billion basic ($67.80 billion diluted) [41, 43, 44].

That steep price drop collides with booming operating numbers. On October 28, 2026, Vertiv reported Q3 2026 sales of $4,312.8 million (+61.2% YoY) and GAAP operating profit of $983.8 million (22.8% margin) [41, 42]. Adjusted operating margin hit 25.2%, while organic orders more than doubled (+100%+ YoY) and 9M adjusted FCF reached $2,230.3 million [41, 42]. Management raised FY2026 guidance to $14,450M–$14,850M in sales, $7.10–$7.20 in adjusted EPS, and $2,600M–$2,800M in adjusted FCF [42]. On November 13, 2026, the Board raised the annual dividend 60% to $0.40 per share [45].

Why did the stock fall 56.25% despite beat-and-raise execution? Five forces drove the de-rating. First, peak valuation above 38x forward earnings left zero room for error [32]. Second, Texas power-grid moratoriums and utility queue delays raised fears of 2027–2028 delivery pushouts [32, 33]. Third, our Pass 1 audit showed 9M capex intensity nearly doubled to 4.2% of sales ($430.3M) while inventories jumped 125.8% YTD to $3,288.4M [41]. Fourth, Vertiv spent >$2.0B upfront on M&A with zero 9M buybacks and carries $239.6M in PurgeRite earnouts plus up to $1.15B in UIG earnouts [41, 43]. Fifth, the broader US equity market entered a Downtrend [51].

web_blocks.html: Multiple compression has removed nearly all speculative premium from the stock. At $380, buyers paid 47x trailing free cash flow for hardware tied to hyperscaler schedules. At $166.24, the market demands 16.75x forward earnings and a 4.88% trailing FCF yield [48]. Next, we test that enterprise value with a Reverse Discounted Cash Flow model. That exercise shows what growth rate $63.59B to $64.68B in EV implies [43, 48].

web_blocks.title: Reverse DCF & Stress Sensitivity: What Does $63.59B–$67.80B EV Assume?
web_blocks.the_number: At $166.24 ($63.59B Finviz EV; $66.52B basic / $67.80B diluted pro-forma EV), a 9.5%-WACC Reverse DCF implies only an 8.3% to 8.9% 10-year FCF CAGR.
web_blocks.how_calculated: Starting from Vertiv's $2.70B FY2026E adjusted FCF midpoint ($2.60B–$2.80B guided), we discount 10 years of FCF at 9.5% baseline WACC (3.0% terminal growth) across 392.7M diluted shares, then stress WACC to 11.5% and normalized FCF0 to $2.10B.
web_blocks.the_inputs: Basic MC $64.01B (385.03M sh) vs. diluted MC $65.28B (392.7M sh) [41, 48]; post-UIG net debt $0.67B [41, 43]; operating leases $428.4M and max earnouts $1.42B ($239.6M PurgeRite + $29.1M 9M + $1,150M UIG; KES undisclosed) [41, 43, 44]; FY26E FCF0 $2.70B vs. normalized FCF0 $2.10B; WACC 9.5% vs. 11.5% (5.04% 10Y Treasury, 2.17 beta) [48, 51].
web_blocks.the_range: Our Base Case (14.5% 10Y FCF CAGR at 9.5% WACC, ~26x FY27E $9.80 EPS) yields ~$255.00/sh, compressing to $186.74 at 11.5% WACC and $199.65 at normalized $2.10B FCF0. Our Bear Case applies a cycle-compression 14.0x multiple on $7.25 FY27E EPS to set $101.50/sh (vs. $76.45 combined DCF bear stress at 11.5% WACC, $2.10B FCF0, 6.5% CAGR, and $2.52B debt-like claims). Our Bull Case (19.0% FCF CAGR) reaches $330.00/sh.
web_blocks.if_off: If FY2027 consensus (+32% revenue, ~$9.92 EPS) holds and inventories unwind cleanly, an 8.3%–8.9% FCF growth bar is conservative. If 11.5% WACC and normalized $2.10B FCF0 prevail alongside grid bottlenecks and earnout cash drains, intrinsic value falls toward $101.50 or the $76.45 combined stress floor.

web_blocks.caption: Table 7.3 — Listed Electrical, Thermal & HVAC Peer Comparison (November 20, 2026)
web_blocks.takeaway: VRT leads the peer group in trailing revenue growth (+35.27%) and operating margin (20.91%) with 23.93% ROIC, yet trades at 16.75x forward P/E—cheaper than ETN, TT, and JCI—while all five peers sit in Stage 4.

web_blocks.html: Comparing VRT against the four active industrial peers in our November 20 snapshot reveals a sector-wide de-rating [48]. Eaton (ETN) earns a 9.84% ROIC and 18.99% operating margin at 19.02x forward P/E [48]. Trane Technologies (TT) posts a 24.17% ROIC and 18.06% operating margin at 21.75x forward P/E [48]. Johnson Controls (JCI) delivers a 12.84% ROIC and 15.60% margin at 17.47x forward P/E [48]. Modine (MOD; tagged under its TradingView feed name) earns 6.41% ROIC and 10.73% margin at 12.63x forward P/E [48]. Vertiv beats ETN, JCI, and MOD on ROIC and operating margin while trading at a discount multiple, yet every peer sits in STAGE_4 [47, 48].

web_blocks.mechanism: Like Vertiv in 2026, Arista Networks grew revenue >30% annually as a core hyperscale supplier at 35x–40x forward earnings. When cloud titans paused switch deployments in 2019 to digest capacity, ANET's growth slowed from +31% in FY18 to +12% in FY19 and -4% in FY20, cutting its multiple from ~38x to ~20x before AI networking sparked a multi-year recovery.
web_blocks.outcome_numbers: ANET dropped ~40% from $330 (split-adjusted ~$20.60) in April 2019 to ~$190 (~$11.90) by late 2019 as forward P/E halved from ~38x to ~20x, before compounding multi-fold from 2021 to 2024.
web_blocks.lesson_for_symbol: Multiple compression from 38x toward 17x forward earnings often reflects capex digestion fear rather than permanent moat failure, but valuation alone never stops a Stage 4 liquidation wave.

web_blocks.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: Cheap Multiples Do Not Catch Falling Knives
paragraphs: On pure business math, paying 16.75x forward earnings for a 23.9% ROIC franchise pricing in only 8.3%–8.5% FCF growth looks tempting. Cash conversion is real, even after accounting for higher 4.2% capex intensity and the $1.45B UIG outlay.
Yet every peer in Table 7.2 is also locked in Stage 4. In Chapter 8, we read the live November 20 tape to see why price action overrides cheap valuation today.

book_paragraphs: Imagine opening your valuation ledger on Friday, November 20, 2026, and placing Vertiv's latest financials beside its closing stock quote. On the fundamentals page, Vertiv just delivered $4.31 billion in third-quarter sales, up 61 percent year-over-year, raised full-year guidance to roughly $14.65 billion in sales and $2.70 billion in adjusted free cash flow, and boosted its regular dividend by 60 percent.

Now look at the stock quote: $166.24, down 10.14 percent in a single session and 56.25 percent below its $379.94 high. At $166.24, Vertiv's basic equity market value across 385.03 million shares stands at $64.01 billion, while diluted market cap across 392.7 million Q3 shares reaches $65.28 billion. Finviz lists enterprise value at $63.59 billion. Adding $1.45 billion of UIG cash lifts post-deal EV to $64.68 billion basic ($65.95 billion diluted). Adding $428.4 million in operating leases and $1.42 billion in maximum contingent earnouts (PurgeRite $239.6 million, nine-month deals $29.1 million, and UIG $1.15 billion, with KES undisclosed) brings full pro-forma EV to $66.52 billion basic or $67.80 billion diluted.

How does an industrial compounder lose more than half its market value during a year of record earnings? Five forces converged at once. First, Vertiv entered 2026 priced above 38 times forward earnings, leaving no room for doubt. Second, utility grid bottlenecks and Texas permitting delays sparked fears of a 2027 or 2028 hyperscaler air-pocket. Third, our Pass 1 audit uncovered two real operational overhangs: nine-month capital spending jumped to 4.2 percent of sales ($430.3 million), and inventories more than doubled to $3.29 billion. Fourth, Vertiv committed over $2.0 billion upfront to six acquisitions with zero share buybacks while carrying up to $1.15 billion in new UIG earnout exposure. Fifth, the broader US market rolled over into a confirmed Downtrend.

book_subsections.title: What $166.24 Implies in Our Reverse DCF Model
paragraphs: Rather than relying on optimistic analyst targets, let us flip the math around. At $63.59 billion to $64.68 billion in enterprise value, how fast does Vertiv's free cash flow need to grow over the next decade to deliver a 9.5 percent annual return?

Starting from Vertiv's $2.70 billion FY2026 free cash flow guidance midpoint and assuming 3.0 percent perpetual growth after year ten, the stock at $166.24 is pricing in only an 8.3 percent to 8.5 percent ten-year compound annual growth rate in free cash flow. Pause on that figure. A business currently growing revenue 35 percent trailing and 61 percent in Q3 is now priced for single-digit cash flow growth over the next decade.

We model three explicit paths plus two harsh sensitivity checks because industrial cycles punish single-point forecasts. In our Bear Case, if utility delays trigger a hyperscaler pause, earnings drop to $7.25 and a cycle-compressed 14.0 times multiple sets downside at $101.50 per share. In our Base Case at 9.5 percent WACC, fair value is $255.00 per share—yet raising WACC to 11.5 percent (against a 5.04 percent 10-year Treasury and 2.17 beta) cuts Base value to $186.74, normalizing FCF0 to $2.10 billion cuts Base value to $199.65, and combining both stresses with 6.5 percent Bear growth and full debt-like claims tests $76.45 per share. In our Bull Case, sustained liquid-cooling expansion supports $330.00 per share.

book_subsections.title: Stacking Vertiv Against Eaton, Trane, Johnson Controls, and Modine
paragraphs: When you place Vertiv beside the four active electrical and thermal peers in our November 20 market snapshot, a vital clue emerges. Eaton trades at 19.02 times forward earnings with a 9.84 percent return on invested capital. Trane Technologies trades at 21.75 times forward earnings with a 24.17 percent return on invested capital. Johnson Controls sits at 17.47 times with a 12.84 percent return, and Modine trades at 12.63 times with a 6.41 percent return.

Vertiv now trades at just 16.75 times forward earnings and 20.51 times trailing free cash flow while earning a 23.93 percent return on invested capital and a 20.91 percent trailing operating margin. Yet every single one of those five peers is currently classified in a Stage 4 downtrend. Institutions are not singling out Vertiv for a company-specific blowup; they are rotating out of the entire data-center electrical and thermal complex at once.

callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
callouts.text: History offers a clear warning from Arista Networks in 2019: great hyperscale suppliers can see their multiples cut in half during capex-digestion scares before eventually recovering. The catch is that nobody rings a bell at the exact bottom of a sector-wide liquidation.

book_subsections.title: Accounting for UIG's Cash Outlay and Earnout Overhang
paragraphs: A disciplined investor adjusts enterprise value for post-quarter deals instead of blindly trusting static screener cards. On September 30, Vertiv held $3.71 billion in cash and short-term investments against $2.93 billion in debt, leaving $783 million in net cash. Twenty-seven days later, Vertiv wired $1.45 billion upfront for UtilityInnovation Group and pledged up to $1.15 billion in future cash earnouts.

Even after subtracting that $1.45 billion cash check—and layering in $428.4 million of operating leases plus $1.42 billion in maximum contingent earnouts across PurgeRite, nine-month bolt-ons, and UIG (with KES undisclosed)—the pro-forma EV reaches $66.52 billion basic or $67.80 billion diluted. At 9.5 percent WACC, $166.24 still prices in single-digit cash flow growth. Yet once you stress WACC to 11.5 percent ($186.74) or normalize FCF0 to $2.10 billion ($199.65), the fundamental margin of safety narrows sharply. That is one more reason why the Stage 4 price tape in Chapter 8 forbids averaging down today.

book_subsections.title: Bridging Q3 2026 Run-Rate to FY2027 Consensus Expectations
paragraphs: Let us sanity-check Wall Street's 2027 earnings estimates against Vertiv's current operating pace. In Q3 2026 alone, Vertiv generated $4.31 billion in sales and 25.2 percent adjusted operating margins. Annualizing that quarter implies roughly $17.25 billion in revenue before any contribution from UtilityInnovation Group or recent capacity expansions in Italy, Malaysia, and North America.

Against that run-rate, consensus expectations for roughly $19.5 billion in 2027 revenue and $9.92 in next-twelve-month earnings per share do not require heroic guesswork. They primarily require hyperscale data-center campuses to receive utility power on schedule so Vertiv can ship its $4.12 billion current deferred revenue backlog.

book_subsections.title: Why Free Cash Flow Yield Matters More Than Trailing GAAP P/E
paragraphs: A surface look at Vertiv's 31.09 times trailing GAAP earnings can mislead investors who ignore purchase-accounting amortization. Trailing GAAP profits absorb more than $200 million per year of non-cash intangible amortization from legacy buyouts and bolt-on acquisitions like CoolTera, PurgeRite, and Great Lakes.

Trailing free cash flow strips away that accounting noise. At $166.24, Vertiv trades at 20.51 times trailing free cash flow—a 4.88 percent cash yield for a business growing trailing sales 35 percent. That fundamental cash floor is why Vertiv belongs high on our watchlist once its Stage 4 downtrend finally ends.
